value: flowering is delayed in a far-red-deficient light environment (pansy is a long-day plant whose flowering responds to far-red light)
method: abstract read from the OpenAlex record's text; authors, volume and pages from the OpenAlex record; the sentence states an earlier finding that the paper builds on

source.title: Photocontrol of flowering and extension growth in the long-day plant pansy
source.journal: Journal of the American Society for Horticultural Science 128(4): 479-485

quote: However, FR-deficient (FRd) environments delay flowering in some long-day plants (LDPs), including `Crystal Bowl Yellow' pansy (Viola ×wittrockiana Gams).
note: Read from the abstract only. The abstract states the delay as background, so the primary measurement is an earlier study that the abstract does not name; the same authors' 2001 paper (10.21273/jashs.126.3.275) tested pansy among five long-day species and is the likely primary source, not confirmed here.

value: two cryptochrome (blue-light receptor) genes, ShCRY1 and ShCRY2, were cloned from chia
method: abstract read from the OpenAlex record's text; cDNA cloning of the genes, which shows the receptor genes are present and does not by itself measure a light response

source.authors: Chen B, Xue Y, Wang B, Shi X, Mei F, Win AN, Chai Y
source.title: Cloning and expression features of cryptochrome genes, ShCRY1 and ShCRY2, from chia (Salvia hispanica)
source.journal: International Journal of Agriculture and Biology 22(5)

quote: Full-length cDNAs of two chia CRY genes, ShCRY1 and ShCRY2, were cloned and investigated, both of which had alternative transcription initiation and poly-A tailing sites.
note: Read from the abstract only. Gene presence, not a measured photoresponse; the abstract also calls cryptochromes blue-light receptors that regulate flowering time through the photoperiod pathway.
